$comment: Decides which changes may merge without a human. Checked into the repo so the policy is reviewable, and read by classify-risk.py. Paths are fnmatch globs against repo-relative paths.
$principle: Fail closed. An unrecognised path is not automatically safe — it is judged by the default rule.
The question is never 'is this change good' (the gates answer that). It is 'if this change is
wrong, how bad is it, and can it be undone'. Anything hard to undo needs a human, however green.

rules.reason: Changes the thing that decides whether changes are safe. A run that can edit its own CI has no CI.
Guardrails and gate definitions. Same reasoning as CI config.
Irreversible or lock-taking schema change. Data removed by a migration is not recoverable from a green test suite.
Additive migration with no destructive statement. Auto-applies on merge; a snapshot is taken first.
Authorisation. A mistake here is silent, and the tests that would catch it are the ones most often missing.
Security headers and edge configuration. Weakening one is invisible in a diff review that is not looking for it.
A new dependency is the highest-consequence thing a run can add, and the thing a prompt-injected agent would most want to add.
Credential-adjacent. Should not appear in a run's diff at all.
Infrastructure. Failure modes are expensive and slow to reverse.
Money. A wrong amount or a double charge is not fixable by reverting the commit.
Published claims and crawler policy. Wrong here is public before anyone notices.
